newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan launches fertiliser plant with India.
newsitem.headline: Jordan launches fertiliser plant with India.

text.p: Jordan and India inaugurated on Monday a $170 million phosphoric acid plant in southern Jordan to supply the Indian market, company officials said.

The project, a joint venture between Jordan Phosphate Mines Company (JMPC) and India's Southern Petrochemicals Industries Company (SPIC), will produce over 200,000 tonnes annually of phosphoric acid at a plant near the major Shidiyeh mine, which provides the basic raw rock phosphate material.

The project, first promoted before the Gulf War, provides the Indian company with a sustained supply of phosphoric acid for its fertiliser plants and at a discount price, while securing for Jordan its long term market and expansion of a growing downstream industry.

The kingdom, a major producer of potash and phosphates, has huge reserves of the rocks, both a main component of fertilisers. It has started expanding its downstream industry to increase the value of its exports.

The project, which is expected to bring Jordan around $80 million a year in exports earnings, is expected to enjoy considerable tax and customs exemptions as the southern area falls under a proposed free zone area.

Earlier this year a joint $85 million Japanese-Jordanian project to produce ammonium phosphates and compound fertiliser began production close to the Red Sea port of Aqaba. It aims to produce eventually 300,000 tonnes of mixed fertilisers annually.
